ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the right triangle $\triangle ABC$ has $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, with $AC=BC=3$. A square $CDEF$ with $C$ as the vertex (the four vertices $C$, $D$, $E$, and $F$ are arranged counterclockwise) can freely rotate around point $C$, and $CD=2$. Connect $AF$ and $BD$. During the rotation of square $CDEF$, what is the minimum value of $BD+\frac{2}{3}AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, take a point \(M\) on \(AC\) such that \(CM=\frac{4}{3}\). Connect \(DM\) and \(AD\).\\
\(\because\) \(CD=2\), \(CM=\frac{4}{3}\), \(CA=3\),\\
\(\therefore\) \(CD^{2}=CM\cdot CA\),\\
\(\therefore\) \(\frac{CD}{CA}=\frac{CM}{CD}\),\\
\(\because\) \(\angle DCM=\angle ACD\),\\
\(\therefore\) \(\triangle DCM \sim \triangle ACD\),\\
\(\therefore\) \(\frac{DM}{AD}=\frac{CD}{AC}=\frac{2}{3}\),\\
\(\therefore\) \(DM=\frac{2}{3}AD\),\\
\(\therefore\) \(BD+\frac{2}{3}AD=BD+DM\),\\
\(\therefore\) when \(B\), \(D\), \(M\) are collinear, the value of \(BD+\frac{2}{3}AD\) is minimized,\\
\(\therefore\) The minimum value = \(\sqrt{CB^{2}+CM^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+(\frac{4}{3})^{2}}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{97}}{3}}\).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, triangle ABC can be seen, in which C is below and slightly to the left, A is directly above C, B is to the right of C, AC and CB are perpendicular, and a right-angle symbol is marked at C. With C as one vertex there is a rotated square CDEF; in the figure D is located to the upper right of C, E is located to the upper left, F is located to the left of C and slightly higher than C, and connecting lines from B to D, from A to F, etc. are drawn. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, AC=BC=3, CD=2. Following the method, construct auxiliary point M, such that M is on AC and CM=4/3. Because CD^2=2^2=4, and CM·CA=(4/3)·3=4, so CD^2=CM·CA, that is CD/CA=CM/CD. Also because M is on AC, ∠DCM and ∠ACD are the same angle formed by CD and AC. Therefore △DCM∼△ACD. From the similarity ratio, DM/AD=CD/AC=2/3, so DM=(2/3)AD. Thus the original expression BD+(2/3)AD can be transformed into BD+DM. By the triangle inequality, BD+DM≥BM, with equality when B, D, M are collinear and D is located between B and M; and on segment BM, the distance to C changes continuously from CM=4/3 to CB=3, so there exists a point D satisfying CD=2, and this collinear position can be reached. Therefore the minimum value is BM. Also BC⊥CM, BC=3, CM=4/3, so BM=sqrt(BC^2+CM^2)=sqrt(3^2+(4/3)^2)=sqrt(97)/3.
